Algeria.d:
Abdelghani Hamel ran Algeria's national police until a 701-kilogram cocaine seizure at the port of Oran in May 2018 exposed the network behind it. A military court and civilian courts later convicted him of corruption and illicit enrichment. Several generals were convicted with him. The convictions are for corruption, not drug trafficking, and Algeria published little about the trafficking case itself.

In 2021 the Pegasus Project, a group of journalists working with Amnesty International, reported that Morocco had chosen more than 6,000 Algerian phones as targets for Pegasus spyware. The targets included politicians and senior military officers. Pegasus is sold by NSO Group. Morocco denied using it. Algeria cut diplomatic relations with Morocco in August 2021 and listed the alleged spying among its reasons.

The Muslim Brotherhood, an Islamist political movement, also has a documented presence in Algeria. Algeria is in the High band of the Global Organized Crime Index.
Algeria.imp: Algerians have no public court account of how cocaine moved through the port of Oran or who protected it. The police chief and generals were punished for enriching themselves, so the trafficking itself was never laid out in court. Politicians and officers whose phones were targeted may have had their calls and messages read by a neighbouring government. The dispute over the spying also helped end diplomatic relations between the two countries.

Angola.d:
In January 2025 a Swiss federal court convicted Trafigura, one of the world's largest oil and metals traders, of bribing an Angolan official. The company paid €4.3 million in 2009–11 to an official linked to a subsidiary of Sonangol, Angola's state oil company. Its former chief operating officer, Mike Wainwright, was also convicted. Trafigura has appealed, so the ruling is not yet final.

Angola's finance minister since October 2019, Vera Daves de Sousa, is listed among alumni of the World Economic Forum's Young Global Leaders programme. The Forum runs the yearly Davos meetings. The programme picks people under about 40 for five years of meetings and courses. Taking part is not wrongdoing.

The Brazilian-run Universal Church of the Kingdom of God built a large following in Angola. Angolan pastors accused its Brazilian leaders of racial discrimination and of pressing pastors into vasectomies. In June 2020 the government dissolved the church's board and removed Bishop Honorilton Gonçalves.

The Gülen movement, a Turkish Islamic network that runs schools abroad, and the Brazilian builder Odebrecht also have a documented presence. The Icelandic fishing company Samherji and the Portuguese bank Banco Espírito Santo are likely present but undocumented.
Angola.imp: Bribes paid at Sonangol came out of Angola's oil business, which is the state's main source of money. The Swiss case shows that a foreign trader paid to win that business, and Angolans learned of it from a court abroad, not at home. Members of the Universal Church lived under foreign leaders whom their own pastors accused of discrimination and of pressure over vasectomies, until the government removed them.

Benin.d: Nothing is documented yet for Benin, so this write-up is a best guess. No case found so far shows a foreign state, company, criminal group or lodge paying or placing people inside its government. The Sovereign Military Order of Malta, a Catholic order that holds diplomatic status, has a documented presence. Two French Masonic bodies, the Grand Orient de France and the Grande Loge Nationale Française (GLNF), are likely present but undocumented. Benin is in the High band of the Global Organized Crime Index.
Benin.imp: Without documented cases, residents cannot know which outside interests, if any, pay or place officials. The High band suggests officials face pressure from criminal and outside interests. If that is so, it would show up in contracts, policing and courts that serve someone other than the public. Residents would pay through lost public money and weaker protection, without a named case to challenge.

Botswana.d: Nothing is documented yet for Botswana, so this write-up is a best guess. No case found so far shows a foreign state, company, criminal group, church or lodge paying or placing people inside its government. No outside organisation is recorded as present either. Botswana is in the Moderate band of the Global Organized Crime Index, lower than most of its neighbours. The lack of cases may reflect limited reporting as well as less outside pressure on officials.
Botswana.imp: Residents have no documented case showing outside interests paying their officials. The Moderate band suggests the risk is smaller than in much of the region, though it is not zero. A case, if one exists, would most likely surface through contracts, licences or policing. Until then, residents have no named official or company to hold to account, and no evidence that public decisions are being bought.

Burkina Faso.d:
Burkina Faso's military government, led by Captain Ibrahim Traoré, ordered French troops out in early 2023. Personnel of Africa Corps, the Russian defence ministry's force in Africa, arrived in January 2024. They set up their first African base at Loumbila, north-east of Ouagadougou. The first group was 100 people, to grow to 300.

Ghana's president alleged that a mine had been given to Wagner, the Russian private military company, as payment. Burkina Faso's mines minister denied it.

The magazine Jeune Afrique reported in 2012 that Blaise Compaoré, president from 1987 to 2014, was a former grand master of the Grande Loge du Burkina. It said his foreign minister, Djibrill Bassolé, had succeeded him in that post. These are press reports, and lodge membership is lawful.

The Gülen movement, a Turkish Islamic network that runs schools abroad, and the Sovereign Military Order of Malta, a Catholic order with diplomatic status, also have a documented presence. Two French Masonic bodies, the Grand Orient de France and the Grande Loge Nationale Française, are likely present but undocumented.
Burkina Faso.imp: The country's army now works with a foreign force that answers to Moscow rather than to Burkina Faso's own voters or courts. If the mine allegation were true, a national resource would be paying for that force, but the minister denies it. Under Compaoré, the president and his foreign minister both led the same lodge, so a private body linked the two men who set foreign policy.

Burundi.d:
BBC Panorama reported in 2015 on leaked records from British American Tobacco (BAT), one of the world's largest tobacco companies. The records name payments to officials in Burundi who handled tobacco control law.

A 2021 analysis by the University of Bath said the payments in Burundi, Comoros, Rwanda and Uganda aimed to block tobacco laws. Those laws were modelled on the WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control, a treaty that commits states to limit tobacco sales and marketing. The UK Serious Fraud Office closed its investigation in 2021 without bringing charges. BAT denies the allegations. These are reports, not court findings.

The Atlas Network, a group that links free-market think tanks, and the Sovereign Military Order of Malta, a Catholic order with diplomatic status, also have a documented presence. Burundi is in the Severe band of the Global Organized Crime Index, which means officials are judged likely to act for outside or criminal interests.
Burundi.imp: If the payments worked as the leaked records suggest, Burundians got weaker tobacco rules than the WHO treaty calls for. That would mean more advertising, cheaper access and fewer warnings, and more smoking-related illness. Because the UK case closed without charges and no Burundian process is recorded, residents do not know which officials were paid or what they did in return.

Cabo Verde.d: Nothing is documented yet for Cabo Verde, so this write-up is a best guess. No case found so far shows a foreign state, company, criminal group or lodge paying or placing people inside its government. The Sovereign Military Order of Malta, a Catholic order that holds diplomatic status, has a documented presence. Cabo Verde is in the Low band of the Global Organized Crime Index. That suggests fewer officials act for outside interests than in most of the region. The lack of cases may also reflect limited reporting.
Cabo Verde.imp: Residents have no documented case of outside interests paying their officials. The Low band suggests courts, police and officials work mostly for the public. If outside money does reach officials, it would most likely show up in ports, shipping or contracts. Residents would then pay through lost public revenue. For now there is no named case, official or company to hold to account.

Cameroon.d:
Cameroon must deposit half its foreign-exchange reserves with the French Treasury. The Bank of Central African States (BEAC), based in Yaoundé, issues the CFA franc for Cameroon, the Central African Republic, Chad, the Republic of Congo, Equatorial Guinea and Gabon. France guarantees the currency's fixed rate to the euro, and the deposit is the condition. West Africa's CFA zone dropped this rule from 2021, but Central Africa still follows it. A French Senate report in December 2024 called the reform incomplete.

Le Monde reported that President Paul Biya gave tens of millions of francs between 1988 and 1992 to OSTI, a Templar order run by Raymond Bernard, and to a related group, CIRCES. It also reported that 11.2 million francs moved from SNH, the state oil company, to Bernard's personal account. The presidency called Bernard an 'old friend' and would not comment on the payments. Bernard was questioned in the Solar Temple inquiry but was not charged. OSTI is listed as based in Cameroon.

The mining and trading company Glencore, the Catholic organisation Opus Dei and a Russian disinformation network tied to Yevgeny Prigozhin also have a documented presence. The Russian Wagner Group and two French Masonic bodies are likely present but undocumented.
Cameroon.imp: Half of the reserves that back Cameroon's money sit with a foreign treasury, so Cameroon cannot decide alone how to use them. If Le Monde's reporting is right, money from the state oil company went into a private order's founder's account instead of public services. Residents have never had an official account of those payments, because the presidency declined to comment.

Central African Republic.d:
About 1,000 fighters from Wagner, a Russian private military company tied to Yevgeny Prigozhin, have been in the Central African Republic since an August 2018 military agreement with Russia. They guarded President Faustin-Archange Touadéra and fought rebels with the national army. Reporting links the deployment to gold, diamond and timber concessions, including a logging operation in Lobaye. Russia's defence ministry is moving these forces under its Africa Corps, and the country remains its largest African deployment.

A Russian, Valery Zakharov, served as Touadéra's security adviser from 2018. Ukraine's security service said he headed Wagner's security firm in the country. The US Treasury put him on its sanctions list and noted he also held a Central African passport.

Reporting from Bangui in July 2026 describes former Wagner members supplying tramadol, a prescription opioid, to the presidential guard and a youth militia. Senior security officials are alleged to control the trade. No one has been charged. The pills come from Indian manufacturers and travel through the Democratic Republic of Congo. Miners take them to work long hours, and fighters take them in combat.

The Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime (GI-TOC) estimates illicit gold exports at $180 million a year. The gold leaves on military cargo planes registered in the country and is laundered through exporters linked to the UAE. A government-backed fuel monopoly also makes unjustified profits. GI-TOC says senior political and military figures, local criminals and foreign groups have joined to control the country's criminal markets.

Earlier, President François Bozizé was reported in 2009 and 2013 to be a Freemason who joined under the sponsorship of Congo's president, Denis Sassou-Nguesso.
Central African Republic.imp: Residents depend on a foreign armed group for the president's safety and for fighting rebels, and that group is paid partly in gold, diamonds and timber. Gold that could earn public revenue leaves the country unrecorded. Tramadol sold to miners and fighters has been linked by university research to more deaths in fighting over mining areas. People also pay inflated fuel prices to a monopoly the government backs.

Chad.d:
A court in N'Djamena sentenced ten people in July 2020 over a tramadol trafficking network that crossed several borders. They included high-ranking security and intelligence officials. Analysts who read the court documents said members used part of the money to try to bribe judges and the security services.

In November 2017 a statement from Chad's presidency said President Idriss Déby had agreed to hand schools run by the Gülen movement to Turkey's state Maarif Foundation. He also agreed to expel people linked to the movement. Turkey's government lists the Gülen movement, a Turkish Islamic network, as a terrorist group.

Chad must deposit half its foreign-exchange reserves with the French Treasury as a member of the Central African CFA franc zone. The regional central bank, BEAC, issues the currency, and France guarantees its fixed rate to the euro.

Déby, president from 1990 to 2021, was named as a Freemason in press reports in 2009 and 2013. No lodge was named. The Sovereign Military Order of Malta, a Catholic order with diplomatic status, also has a documented presence. Chad is in the Severe band of the Global Organized Crime Index.
Chad.imp: When senior army and intelligence officers take part in drug trafficking, the agencies that should stop the trade include some of the people running it. Chadians then rely on courts and police that the same network tried to bribe. Families whose children attended Gülen schools saw the schools change hands at a foreign government's request. Part of the national reserves sits with a foreign treasury.

Comoros.d:
Under a 2008 'economic citizenship' law, Comoros sold its passports in bulk to stateless people, called bidoon, living in Gulf states. Gulf money paid for them. The Syrian-French businessman Bashar Kiwan ran the scheme with the government. Prosecutors said it brought in about $200 million, much of which never reached the treasury.

In November 2022 a court in Moroni sentenced former president Ahmed Abdallah Sambi to life in prison for high treason and related charges. Kiwan was tried with him.

In 2015 BBC Panorama reported that British American Tobacco (BAT) arranged bribes for officials in Rwanda, Burundi and Comoros. The reporting used documents from a former BAT employee, Paul Hopkins. Some payments aimed to block tobacco control laws based on a World Health Organization treaty. The UK Serious Fraud Office closed its investigation in January 2021 without charges. BAT denied wrongdoing.

The Sovereign Military Order of Malta, a Catholic order with diplomatic status, also has a documented presence. Comoros is in the High band of the Global Organized Crime Index.
Comoros.imp: Comorians lost most of the money their passports earned, according to prosecutors. Thousands of people now hold Comorian citizenship bought by Gulf money, which weakens what the passport means for those born there. If the tobacco payments worked as reported, residents also got weaker rules on tobacco sales and advertising than the WHO treaty sets.

Congo, Dem. Rep..d:
M23 is an armed group that took the eastern city of Goma in January 2025, and Bukavu after it. UN investigators reported in June 2025 that M23 operates under Rwandan command and that Rwandan army reinforcements backed the capture of Goma. They said M23 appointed new governors in North and South Kivu. They also said it put Rwandans in charge of mining, tax, banking and border control, and removed 18 customary chiefs. Rwanda denies directing M23.

US authorities said Glencore, a Swiss-based commodity trader and one of Congo's largest miners, paid $27.5 million to third parties from 2007 to 2018. They said part of it was meant to bribe Congolese officials. Glencore later agreed to pay Congo $180 million to settle the claims.

In 2017 the US Treasury sanctioned Dan Gertler, an Israeli mining and oil investor and long-time friend of former president Joseph Kabila. It said he made a fortune through corrupt mining and oil deals using that friendship. Under a later settlement his Ventora group returned licences and agreed to pay royalties to the state miner Gécamines. Gertler denies wrongdoing.

Erik Prince, who founded the US military contractor Blackwater, sent men and drones in February 2026 to help Congo's army secure the eastern city of Uvira, Reuters reported. A Russian disinformation network tied to Yevgeny Prigozhin also has a documented presence.
Congo, Dem. Rep..imp: In North and South Kivu, people now live under governors, tax collectors and border officials appointed by an armed group, according to the UN. Customary chiefs they relied on were removed. Across the country, payments to officials and insiders meant mining wealth went to private hands instead of the state budget. The settlements paid some of it back, but only after foreign investigations forced them.

Congo, Rep..d:
Denis Sassou-Nguesso, president of the Republic of Congo, is reported to be Grand Master of the Grand Lodge of Congo-Brazzaville. That lodge is linked to the Grande Loge Nationale Française (GLNF), a French Masonic body. Afrik-News reported this in 2009, and Jeune Afrique in 2013. A 2013 Jeune Afrique report also said the Central African Republic's president, François Bozizé, joined Freemasonry under Sassou-Nguesso's sponsorship. Lodge membership is lawful, and these are press reports.

Congo must deposit half its foreign-exchange reserves with the French Treasury as a member of the Central African CFA franc zone. In return France guarantees the currency's fixed rate to the euro. West Africa dropped the deposit rule from 2021, but it still applies here.

The commodity trader Gunvor and the Sovereign Military Order of Malta, a Catholic order with diplomatic status, have a documented presence. The oil company Eni is likely present but undocumented.

Earlier, Jeune Afrique reported in 2012 that Pascal Lissouba, president from 1992 to 1997, had been initiated at a lodge of the Grand Orient de France in Besançon. The Grand Orient is France's largest Masonic body.
Congo, Rep..imp: When the president also heads a lodge tied to a French body, senior officials and foreign contacts can meet in a private setting that voters cannot see. The reports do not show what decisions came from it. Half of the reserves that back the country's money sit with the French Treasury, so Congolese governments cannot decide alone how to use them.

Cote d'Ivoire.d:
Jeune Afrique reported in 2012 that Prime Minister Jeannot Ahoussou-Kouadio and Interior Minister Hamed Bakayoko were Freemasons. It said the state prosecutor, Simplice Koffi Kouadio, had been received by the Grande Loge de Côte d'Ivoire. It added that President Alassane Ouattara was not officially known to be a member. These are press reports, and lodge membership is lawful.

In October 2019 Facebook removed fake accounts run by a network tied to Yevgeny Prigozhin, a Russian businessman. The network targeted Côte d'Ivoire and seven other African countries.

Glencore and Gunvor, two large commodity traders, have a documented presence. So do Opus Dei, a Catholic organisation, and the Sovereign Military Order of Malta, a Catholic order with diplomatic status. Two French Masonic bodies, the Grand Orient de France and the Grande Loge Nationale Française, are likely present but undocumented.

Côte d'Ivoire is in the Moderate band of the Global Organized Crime Index. No documented case so far shows a foreign state or company paying Ivorian officials.
Cote d'Ivoire.imp: When the prime minister, the interior minister and the state prosecutor belong to or meet the same lodge, residents cannot see whether lodge ties affect appointments or prosecutions. The reports do not show that they did. Fake accounts run from abroad fed Ivorians false or slanted political news under false identities.

Djibouti.d:
China opened its first overseas military base in Djibouti in 2017. A subsidiary of China Merchants bought 23.5% of the Port of Djibouti in 2013.

A US Congressional Research Service brief said in June 2025 that Chinese institutions hold over half of Djibouti's $2.6 billion external debt. That includes a $1.2 billion loan from China's Exim Bank.

Djibouti suspended repayments in 2022 and later agreed a pause. US officials have warned that the debt 'could give Beijing undue leverage'. Djibouti says it will not hand control of its port to China. These are concerns and statements, not findings of wrongdoing.

Ericsson, the Swedish telecoms equipment maker, admitted paying about €2.1 million to high-ranking Djibouti officials. The payments won it a contract with Djibouti Telecom, the state telephone company. The admission came in a 2019 settlement of US criminal and civil cases. Under that settlement Ericsson paid more than $1 billion over corruption in five countries.

Djibouti is in the Moderate band of the Global Organized Crime Index.
Djibouti.imp: Djibouti owes most of its foreign debt to one country, which also has a military base and a stake in its main port. If the government cannot repay, that country can press for concessions. Residents paid for a telephone contract won with bribes to their officials, and learned of it from a US court settlement.

Egypt.d:
Mohamed Morsi, a senior figure in the Muslim Brotherhood, an Islamist movement, won Egypt's presidential election in June 2012. The army removed him in July 2013. Most Brotherhood leaders were jailed in the following months.

In December 2013 the interim cabinet declared the Brotherhood a terrorist organisation, two days after a car bomb at the Mansoura police headquarters. A different group, Ansar Bait al-Maqdis, claimed that bombing. Membership can now bring up to five years in prison.

Morsi was accused of passing state secrets to Qatar while he was president. In 2017 Egypt's top appeals court upheld his life sentence for leading an illegal group. It threw out a separate term for stealing secret documents. Qatar denied the accusations.

Hizb ut-Tahrir, an Islamist party, the Gülen movement and the Unification Church also have a documented presence. Egypt's General Intelligence Service is based in the country.

Today's arrangements also have older roots. After Khedive Ismail went bankrupt in 1876, Britain and France took control of Egypt's finances for its European creditors. Evelyn Baring, of the Barings banking family, became the British controller, although Barings Bank held Egyptian debt. From 1883 to 1907 he ran Egypt as Britain's agent and consul-general. In 1976 Egypt's intelligence chief signed the charter of the Safari Club, a pact of five intelligence services.
Egypt.imp: Egyptians who voted for Morsi saw him removed by the army. Anyone linked to the Brotherhood can now face prison for membership alone. The Qatar case shows the state treating a rival Gulf government as an enemy, with life sentences attached. In the colonial period, Egypt's revenues went first to its European creditors, under a controller whose family bank held the debt.

Equatorial Guinea.d:
Teodoro Obiang has ruled Equatorial Guinea since 1979. In autumn 2024 Russia sent up to 200 Africa Corps troops to protect his presidency, according to the CTC Sentinel and other analyses. The troops also train elite units in Malabo and Bata. Africa Corps is the Russian defence ministry's force in Africa.

Obiang officially received the Africa Corps commander in Malabo in November 2025. The visit made public a military partnership that analysts had reported a year earlier.

Equatorial Guinea must deposit half its foreign-exchange reserves with the French Treasury as a member of the Central African CFA franc zone. The regional central bank, BEAC, issues the currency. France guarantees its fixed rate to the euro.

Glencore, the mining and commodity trading company, has a documented presence. So does the Sovereign Military Order of Malta, a Catholic order with diplomatic status. Equatorial Guinea is in the Severe band of the Global Organized Crime Index.
Equatorial Guinea.imp: Foreign soldiers now protect a president who has held power since 1979, which makes it harder for Equatoguineans to change their leadership. Elite units trained by Russia owe part of their skills to a foreign government. Half of the reserves that back the country's money sit with a foreign treasury.

Eritrea.d: Nothing is documented yet for Eritrea, so this write-up is a best guess. No case found so far names a foreign state, company or criminal group paying or placing people in Eritrean offices. The Sovereign Military Order of Malta, a Catholic order that holds diplomatic status, has a documented presence. Eritrea is in the Severe band of the Global Organized Crime Index. That band means officials are judged likely to act for outside or criminal interests. The lack of cases may reflect limited reporting.
Eritrea.imp: Residents have no documented case to point to. The Severe band suggests officials often serve outside or criminal interests rather than the public. If so, it would show in smuggling, contracts and policing that people cannot challenge. Residents would pay through lost public money and weaker protection. Without a named case, there is no official or company they can hold to account.

Eswatini.d: Nothing is documented yet for Eswatini, so this write-up is a best guess. No case found so far shows a foreign state, company, criminal group, church or lodge paying or placing people inside its government. No outside organisation is recorded as present. Eswatini is in the High band of the Global Organized Crime Index. That band means officials are judged likely to act for outside or criminal interests. The lack of cases may reflect limited reporting.
Eswatini.imp: Residents have no documented case of outside interests paying their officials. The High band suggests such pressure exists. If it does, it would most likely show in contracts, licences and policing that residents cannot easily question. People would pay through lost public money and weaker protection. Without a named case, there is no official or company to hold to account.

Ethiopia.d:
China built and paid for the African Union headquarters in Addis Ababa, which opened in 2012. Huawei, the Chinese telecoms company, supplied most of its computer and network equipment. In January 2018 Le Monde reported that AU staff had found the building's computers sending data to servers in Shanghai every night. Microphones were also found hidden in walls and furniture.

The AU replaced its servers and declined Chinese offers to set up new ones. China called the report 'ridiculous'. Huawei said its equipment was not the source. No backdoor has been publicly shown.

Ethiopia's prime minister, Abiy Ahmed, is a Pentecostal Christian. He attends and sometimes preaches at the Ethiopian Full Gospel Believers' Church. He became prime minister in 2018 and in 2019 formed the Prosperity Party, which governs today. Religious belief is lawful.

The Tony Blair Institute, which advises governments, and Huawei have a documented presence. So does the conservative family-policy group Family Watch International. The Gülen movement, a Turkish Islamic network, is likely present. Ethiopia is in the Moderate band of the Global Organized Crime Index.
Ethiopia.imp: If the AU reports are right, African governments meeting in Addis Ababa had their internal data copied abroad for years. Ethiopian staff and visitors worked in a building that may have recorded them. The AU replaced its servers, but it cannot know what was taken. Abiy's religion is a private matter; whether it shapes policy is not shown.

Gabon.d:
Omar Bongo, president of Gabon from 1967 until his death in 2009, founded two Masonic bodies. One was linked to the Grand Orient de France, France's largest Masonic body. The other, the Grand Lodge of Gabon, was linked to the Grande Loge Nationale Française (GLNF). He held the grand mastership until he died.

In 2009 the GLNF's Grand Master, François Stifani, installed Bongo's son Ali as Grand Master. Ali Bongo became president the same year. He kept the lodge post until after the August 2023 coup. Jeune Afrique reported that ministers and the head of the National Security Council attended his installation. It also reported that police chief Antoine Embinga, grand master of another lodge, was removed in 2012.

After the coup, the Grand Lodge of Gabon chose Jacques Denis Tsanga, a provincial governor, as grand master. Transitional leader Brice Oligui Nguema reportedly declined the post. In November 2023 the Grand Orient de France's Grand Master, Guillaume Trichard, met Oligui in secret in Libreville and offered support, Gabonreview reported. Oligui was elected president in April 2025.

Gabon must also deposit half its foreign-exchange reserves with the French Treasury as a member of the Central African CFA franc zone. Lodge membership is lawful.
Gabon.imp: For more than 50 years the head of state also led the country's main lodge, tied to a French body. Ministers and security chiefs attended its ceremonies. Gabonese voters had no way to see what was agreed there. After the coup, a French lodge leader met the new ruler in secret. Part of the national reserves sits in Paris.

Gambia.d:
Under President Yahya Jammeh, Lebanese businessmen whom the US designates as Hezbollah financiers received state monopolies. Hezbollah is a Lebanese Shia party and armed group. OCCRP, a network of investigative reporters, showed that Mohamed Bazzi was one of Jammeh's closest associates and got monopolies including the fuel supply.

Ali Charara, also designated by the US, paid $35 million for half of the state telecoms firms Gamtel and Gamcel. OCCRP estimated that over $100 million from Gambian telecoms reached Hezbollah. Jammeh left office in 2017.

Between 2014 and 2017 The Gambia exported nearly $163 million of rosewood to China, though its own rosewood was almost gone. Most came from Senegal's Casamance region, where logging pays for armed groups. Westwood Company held the exclusive export licence.

The Swiss group TRIAL International says Jammeh co-founded Westwood with Swiss national Nicolae Bogdan Buzaianu. It filed a criminal complaint for pillage with the Swiss Attorney General in 2019. This is an allegation, not a verdict.

The Mouride Brotherhood, a Sufi order, also has a documented presence.
Gambia.imp: Gambians paid for fuel and phone services through monopolies handed to the president's associates. Money from those services went abroad instead of to the state, according to OCCRP. The rosewood trade earned money for a company the president is alleged to have co-founded, while logging in neighbouring Casamance paid for armed groups near Gambia's border.

Ghana.d:
At his parliamentary vetting in January 2025, George Opare Addo said he was a Freemason and named his lodge, Amity. He was then confirmed as Minister for Youth Development and Empowerment. The man who asked him, Alexander Afenyo-Markin, had said the year before that he was 'a Freemason and a Catholic'.

In May 2024 GhanaWeb reported that National Security Minister Albert Kan-Dapaah and Transport Minister Kweku Ofori Asiamah took part as members in a Grand Lodge of Ghana event. The event honoured the Asantehene, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, for 25 years in Freemasonry. Former President John Kufuor has said he joined in 1967. Lodge membership is lawful.

In 2006 seventy-seven parcels of cocaine landed from the vessel MV Benjamin and then disappeared. A recording surfaced of a senior police officer meeting suspects at his home. A committee led by a Supreme Court judge found the police account unsatisfactory. The officer returned to duty.

The Tony Blair Institute, which advises governments, and the aircraft maker Airbus have a documented presence. The United Grand Lodge of England and the Atlas Network, which links free-market think tanks, are likely present but undocumented. Ghana is in the High band of the Global Organized Crime Index.
Ghana.imp: When ministers, a former president and the country's leading traditional ruler share a lodge, residents cannot see whether lodge ties affect who gets appointed. Ghanaians lost a large cocaine shipment from police custody and saw the officer involved go back to work. That leaves people unsure whether police will act against traffickers.

Guinea.d:
Simandou, in Guinea, holds one of the world's largest untapped iron ore deposits. In 2008 the government took two blocks there from Rio Tinto and gave them to BSG Resources, controlled by Israeli businessman Beny Steinmetz. In January 2021 a Geneva court found Steinmetz guilty of bribing Mamadie Touré, a wife of President Lansana Conté, to get the rights.

The court sentenced Steinmetz to five years in prison. Swiss appeal courts upheld the conviction. He denies wrongdoing.

Conté's son, Ousmane Conté, was arrested in February 2009 by the junta that took power after his father died. He confessed on state television to involvement in the cocaine trade. It is unclear whether the confession was coerced. The US Treasury designated him a drug kingpin in 2010. No court verdict followed.

Jeune Afrique reported in 2012 that President Alpha Condé oversaw the Grande Loge de Guinée. In 2017 Guinea handed Gülen-linked schools to Turkey's state Maarif Foundation after talks with Turkey's foreign ministry. The Tony Blair Institute, which advises governments, also has a documented presence.
Guinea.imp: Guineans lost control of one of the world's largest iron ore deposits for years after rights were obtained through a bribe to the president's wife. The money that should have come from the deposit went elsewhere. The president's own son confessed to cocaine trafficking, and no Guinean court ever ruled on it.

Guinea-Bissau.d:
Since the mid-2000s Guinea-Bissau has been a transit point for South American cocaine headed to Europe. In April 2013 the US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) arrested former navy chief José Américo Bubo Na Tchuto at sea in a sting. He pleaded guilty in New York to conspiring to import cocaine.

The air force chief, Ibraima Papa Camara, was indicted in the same case. Army chief General António Indjai, who led the 2012 coup, was charged with offering to store cocaine for the FARC, a Colombian guerrilla group. He was also charged with offering to sell it weapons, including surface-to-air missiles. Camara and Indjai stayed in Bissau and were never handed over.

In 2022 President Umaro Sissoco Embaló blamed Na Tchuto, back home by then, for a failed attack on the government palace.

In March 2009 President João Bernardo Vieira and the army chief of staff were killed within hours of each other. No one was prosecuted. UN bodies linked the killings to the cocaine trade, but no court has.

In February 2022 the head of the judicial police said 975 of 980 kilograms of cocaine seized in November 2021 had vanished from official custody. Police and security staff were suspected, and one officer was arrested. The country had not tried a drug case since 2005.
Guinea-Bissau.imp: The heads of the navy, air force and army have all faced US drug charges, and two of them stayed in post or at home without trial. Residents live with armed forces whose commanders were accused of working for traffickers. A president was killed with no prosecution. Seized cocaine disappears from police custody, so arrests rarely lead to trials.

Kenya.d:
In Mombasa, a heroin business paid Kenyan judges, prosecutors and police for two years to stop its owners being sent to the United States. The two Akasha brothers who ran it admitted this in a New York court in 2018. None of those officials has been named or charged in Kenya.

In 2011 the US designated Harun Mwau, a sitting MP and assistant transport minister in charge of the Ports Authority, as a drug kingpin. He resigned and denies the allegations. A police inquiry, which researchers called controversial, cleared him.

Cambridge Analytica, a British political-data firm, said in 2018 that it ran Uhuru Kenyatta's 2013 and 2017 campaigns and wrote his party's manifesto. In 2023 reporters filmed the head of Team Jorge, an Israeli hacking firm, showing access to the Telegram account of Dennis Itumbi. Itumbi ran digital strategy for William Ruto's 2022 campaign and confirmed the account had been hacked.

In October 2024 Kenya returned four Turkish refugees linked to the Gülen movement to Turkey, 'at the request of the government of Türkiye'. The UN said it was 'deeply concerned'. Turkish intelligence had seized Gülen's nephew in Kenya in 2021.

Patrick Njoroge, a celibate member of Opus Dei, governed the Central Bank of Kenya from 2015 to 2023. President Ruto plans to build a church for 8,000 people at State House with his own money. In November 2024 he cancelled the Adani Group's airport and power deals after its directors were charged with bribery in New York.

Earlier, the International Criminal Court charged Kenyatta with organising attacks by Mungiki, a banned sect, during the 2007–08 post-election violence. Prosecutors withdrew the charges in 2014, citing witness interference.
Kenya.imp: Kenyans rely on judges, prosecutors and police, some of whom a heroin business paid and who have never been named. Their elections were run partly by foreign data firms, and a winning campaign's accounts were hacked from abroad. Refugees who sought safety in Kenya were sent back to a government they had fled. Victims of the 2007–08 violence never saw a trial.

Lesotho.d: Nothing is documented yet for Lesotho, so this write-up is a best guess. No case found so far shows a foreign state, company, criminal group or lodge paying or placing people inside its government. The Sovereign Military Order of Malta, a Catholic order that holds diplomatic status, has a documented presence. Lesotho is in the High band of the Global Organized Crime Index. That band means officials are judged likely to act for outside or criminal interests. The lack of cases may reflect limited reporting.
Lesotho.imp: Residents have no documented case of outside interests paying their officials. The High band suggests such pressure exists. If it does, it would most likely show in contracts, licences and policing that residents cannot easily question. People would pay through lost public money and weaker protection. Without a named case, there is no official or company to hold to account.

Liberia.d:
In 2026 Liberian police seized close to four tonnes of cocaine bound for Europe, the country's largest recorded seizure. The police inspector general then said senior government officials were involved in trafficking. Police charged the head of their Major Crimes Unit and another official. They named a deputy commander responsible for security at Roberts International Airport as an active participant.

Twelve suspects were charged in the seizure case. A former vice-president was separately indicted on trafficking counts. These are charges, not convictions.

In 2010 South American and West African traffickers paid senior Liberian officials for safe passage and storage of cocaine. The officials reported the approaches and worked with the US Drug Enforcement Administration. That led to extraditions and convictions in New York.

Older arrangements also left their mark. William Tolbert, president from 1971 to 1980, was Grand Master of the Masonic Order of Liberia. Lodge membership was widely seen as a requirement for leadership in the ruling True Whig Party. Tolbert was killed in Samuel Doe's 1980 coup, and Doe banned the order. Doe later lifted the ban and was initiated himself in 1989.

The National Endowment for Democracy, a US-funded body, and the Tony Blair Institute have a documented presence.
Liberia.imp: If the 2026 charges hold, the police unit meant to fight major crime and the officer guarding the main airport were working with traffickers. Residents cannot rely on those offices to stop drugs moving through the country. The 2010 case shows officials can refuse such payments and help prosecutions instead.

Libya.d:
Khalifa Haftar's Libyan National Army controls eastern Libya. In 2020 UN monitors counted 800–1,200 fighters from Wagner, a Russian private military company, supporting it. A 2020 Pentagon report said the UAE was Wagner's main funder in Libya. Since spring 2024 Russia's Africa Corps has been replacing Wagner, and Russia uses eastern bases as supply hubs.

A UN panel found in 2021 that Erik Prince, founder of the US contractor Blackwater, broke the UN arms embargo. In 2019 he tried to supply aircraft and men to Haftar's forces. Prince denies it.

In Tripoli, Khalid al-Mishri chaired the High Council of State, the upper advisory body of the Tripoli-based government, from 2018 to 2023. He belongs to the Justice and Construction Party, the political arm of the Libyan Muslim Brotherhood.

Libyan authorities buy fuel at world prices and sell it at home for about 0.15 dinars a litre. Smugglers resell it abroad. Crisis Group says officials in both Tripoli and Benghazi take income from this trade, which helps keep the peace between them. UN rules let ships be stopped only if Libya's government flags a cargo, and it has not done so in years.

A coast guard commander at Zawiya, Abd al-Rahman Milad, known as Bija, was sanctioned by the UN in 2018 for fuel smuggling, migrant trafficking and violence at sea. He was released without conviction in 2021. In 2020 the US sanctioned a Libyan operator, a company registered in Malta and a vessel for smuggling fuel and drugs.
Libya.imp: Libyans pay for a fuel subsidy that smugglers and officials resell abroad for profit. Foreign fighters and weapons have kept the country split between two governments. Migrants at sea depend on a coast guard whose commander was sanctioned for trafficking and violence. The US sanctioned Wagner over landmines planted around Tripoli, where people still live.

Madagascar.d:
In Madagascar's 2018 presidential election, Russian political strategists tied to Yevgeny Prigozhin worked with as many as eight candidates. The Russian outlet Proekt and the BBC reported this in 2019. Prigozhin was the businessman behind the Wagner Group, a Russian private military company.

Candidate André Mailhol said the strategists gave him €5,000 in cash. Former prime minister Omer Beriziky said he was promised $2 million. The winner, Andry Rajoelina, denied being Russia's candidate, and the BBC found no evidence he took Russian money. Prigozhin's representatives denied any link.

In October 2019 Facebook removed fake accounts tied to Prigozhin. They had targeted Madagascar's election, along with politics in seven other African countries.

The Sovereign Military Order of Malta, a Catholic order with diplomatic status, has a documented presence. Two French Masonic bodies, the Grand Orient de France and the Grande Loge Nationale Française, are likely present but undocumented. Madagascar is in the High band of the Global Organized Crime Index.
Madagascar.imp: Malagasy voters chose a president in a race where foreign strategists paid or promised money to several candidates. They read political news shaped by fake accounts run from abroad. No court or official inquiry has set out who took money and what they offered in return. Residents cannot tell whether the people they elected owe anything to a foreign backer.

Malawi.d:
In June 2022 Malawi's Anti-Corruption Bureau reported that the police and the Malawi Defence Force gave 16 contracts to five companies linked to Zuneth Sattar. Sattar is a UK-based businessman. The contracts were worth over $150 million and ran from 2017 to 2021.

President Lazarus Chakwera said 84 people were named in the report. He withdrew all delegated powers from Vice President Saulos Chilima. Former police chief George Kainja and lands minister Kezzie Msukwa were arrested. Chilima denied wrongdoing. He died in a plane crash in June 2024.

These are findings of an investigation and arrests, not convictions. The contracts covered supplies for the police and army, so a single outside businessman became a main supplier to both security forces.

British American Tobacco is likely present but undocumented. Malawi is in the Moderate band of the Global Organized Crime Index.
Malawi.imp: Malawians paid, through their taxes, for security contracts the anti-corruption bureau linked to one businessman. Money meant for the police and army went to his companies. Residents now wait for courts to decide whether the vice president, police chief and a minister took part. Until then, it is unclear what the public got for that money.

Mali.d:
Africa Corps is the Russian defence ministry's unit that took over most of Wagner's African work after Yevgeny Prigozhin died in 2023. Wagner left Mali in June 2025. Africa Corps is now the only Russian force there, with about 2,000 troops. Human Rights Watch and Le Monde have reported killings of civilians by Malian soldiers and Africa Corps members in 2025–26.

In July 2023 the US Treasury sanctioned Mali's defence minister, Colonel Sadio Camara, saying he arranged Wagner's deployment. It also sanctioned the air force chief, Colonel Alou Boi Diarra, and his deputy, Lieutenant Colonel Adama Bagayoko. A sanction is one government's decision, not a verdict.

Cocaine seizures across Mali and four neighbouring Sahel states rose from about 13 kilograms a year to 1,466 kilograms in 2022. The UN found the proceeds going into gold and real estate, and named armed groups in Mali among those who gained. No prosecution has followed.

In 2009 a Boeing 727 from Venezuela was unloaded at a desert strip near Tarkint and then burned. UN and Malian investigations pointed to protection by local officials and armed groups. No senior figure was convicted.

Jeune Afrique reported in 2012 that President Amadou Toumani Touré oversaw the Grande Loge du Mali.
Mali.imp: Malians live under a military government whose security depends on foreign troops reported to have killed civilians. Cocaine money goes into gold and property and pays armed groups. With no prosecutions, residents see traffickers and their protectors go unpunished. Civilians in conflict areas face killings that Human Rights Watch and Le Monde attribute to soldiers and Africa Corps members.

Mauritania.d: Nothing is documented yet for Mauritania, so this write-up is a best guess. No case found so far shows a foreign state, company or criminal group paying or placing people inside its government. The Gülen movement, a Turkish Islamic network, the Muslim Brotherhood, an Islamist movement, and the human rights group Fight Impunity have a documented presence. So does the Sovereign Military Order of Malta. Mauritania is in the High band of the Global Organized Crime Index.
Mauritania.imp: Residents have no documented case of outside interests paying their officials. The High band suggests such pressure exists. Mauritania sits on the Sahel cocaine route, so it would most likely show in policing and border control. Residents would then face traffickers protected by officials. Without a named case, there is no official or company to hold to account.

Mauritius.d:
In June 2020 the African Development Bank barred Burmeister & Wain Scandinavian Contractor, a Danish power-plant builder, from its projects for 21 months. During that time it could not bid on work the bank funds. The bank found 'on the balance of probabilities' that the company paid members of the Mauritian administration through middlemen.

The payments came during tenders for the Saint-Louis power station of the Central Electricity Board, the state power company. A debarment is a lender's decision, not a court verdict. The bank's decision names no Mauritian official.

The Grand Orient de France, France's largest Masonic body, has a documented presence. So does the Sovereign Military Order of Malta, a Catholic order with diplomatic status. The Grande Loge Nationale Française, the Hindu nationalist group RSS and the aircraft maker Airbus are likely present but undocumented. Mauritius is in the Moderate band of the Global Organized Crime Index.
Mauritius.imp: Mauritians pay for electricity from a power station whose builder was found to have paid officials during the tender. Because no official was named, residents do not know who was paid. The officials who took part in the tender may still work in the public service. The case came to light through a foreign lender's process, not a Mauritian court.

Morocco.d:
In June 2026 a Casablanca court sentenced 29 people in the 'Escobar of the Sahara' case. They included a former regional council president, who got 12 years, and two former MPs from the governing party. The case began when a jailed Malian trafficker said his Moroccan political associates had seized his assets. It covered cannabis resin and cocaine moved across North Africa. Appeals are open.

The 2021 Pegasus Project reported that Morocco selected more than 6,000 Algerian phones as targets for Pegasus spyware. Le Monde reported that Morocco also selected President Macron of France and 14 French ministers. Morocco denied using Pegasus.

Ahmed Toufiq has been the king's Minister of Islamic Affairs since 2002. He follows the Boutchichiya, Morocco's largest Sufi order. From 2011 to 2021 the Justice and Development Party (PJD), an Islamist party historically linked to the Muslim Brotherhood, led the government. Morocco shut Gülen-linked schools in 2017.

In 1976 Morocco's foreign intelligence chief, General Ahmed Dlimi, signed the charter of the Safari Club, a pact of five intelligence services. In 1977 France flew Moroccan troops into Zaire to defend Mobutu.
Morocco.imp: Moroccans elected legislators from the governing party who were later convicted in a drug and gold trafficking case. The trial showed politicians working with traffickers rather than against them. Residents also live under a state reported to use spyware against foreign officials, which raises the question of who else it targets. The convictions are under appeal.

Mozambique.d:
In 2013–14 three Mozambican state companies borrowed about $2 billion from Credit Suisse, Russia's VTB bank and others. The loans were backed by state guarantees never shown to parliament or the IMF. They paid for tuna fishing and maritime security projects with the shipbuilder Privinvest.

US prosecutors said at least $200 million went in bribes and kickbacks to bankers and officials. A Brooklyn jury convicted former finance minister Manuel Chang in 2024. Prosecutors said Privinvest paid him $7 million.

When the hidden loans came to light in 2016, the IMF and World Bank froze support. Credit Suisse pleaded guilty to fraud in the US and forgave $200 million of Mozambique's debt. Mozambique's Constitutional Council declared the loans void.

Researchers in 2018 described heroin trafficking through Mozambique for three decades, with close ties between ruling party figures and traffickers. They pointed to almost no heroin seizures. In 2010 the US named a leading Maputo businessman a drug kingpin and designated his conglomerate, Grupo MBS, and the Maputo Shopping Centre. Banks closed their branches in the mall within a month. He was never prosecuted.

In 2019 Facebook removed fake accounts tied to Yevgeny Prigozhin's Russian network that targeted Mozambique's October election.
Mozambique.imp: Mozambicans were left owing billions in debt that their parliament never approved. When it came to light, foreign aid stopped, and one study estimated two million people were pushed into poverty. Heroin passed through the country for decades with almost no seizures, which points to protection from officials. Voters also faced fake news run from Russia during an election.

Namibia.d:
In November 2019 WikiLeaks published files about Samherji, one of Iceland's largest fishing companies. The files and Samherji's former Namibia manager, Jóhannes Stefánsson, said the company paid Namibian officials for horse-mackerel fishing quotas.

Fisheries Minister Bernhardt Esau and Justice Minister Sacky Shanghala resigned the next day. In December 2019 they and four associates, called the 'Fishrot Six', were arrested. They face charges of racketeering, corruption and money laundering under Namibia's organised crime law.

Iceland opened its own investigation. Samherji denies paying bribes and blames Stefánsson. The case is still before Namibian courts, so no one has been convicted.

The Mwalimu Julius Nyerere Leadership School, a training school for ruling parties in the region, has a documented presence. So does the Sovereign Military Order of Malta, a Catholic order with diplomatic status. The Afrikaner Broederbond, a secret Afrikaner society, is likely present but undocumented. Namibia is in the Moderate band of the Global Organized Crime Index.
Namibia.imp: Namibia's fish belong to the public, and quotas decide who may catch them. If the charges are proved, two ministers sold that access to a foreign company. Local fishing firms and workers lost quota, and the state lost income it would have earned. Residents have waited years for the courts to rule.

Niger.d:
After the July 2023 coup, Niger's military government ended military cooperation with the United States and France. Dozens of Africa Corps troops, from the Russian defence ministry, arrived in Niamey in April 2024. They were stationed at Air Base 101 before US forces had left it. Estimates for 2025 put them at 200–300, mostly in intelligence, training and surveillance.

In 2017 Niger handed Gülen-linked schools to Turkey's state Maarif Foundation after talks with Turkey's foreign ministry. The Gülen movement is a Turkish Islamic network that Turkey's government lists as a terrorist group.

Niger lies on a Sahel route that UNODC, the UN drugs office, calls a natural stopover for cocaine between South America and Europe. In 2021 a local mayor was arrested with more than 200 kilograms of cocaine in his vehicle. No outcome is documented.

Mamadou Tandja, president from 1999 to 2010, was named as a Freemason in 2009 press reports. No lodge was named. The influence firm Archimedes Group and the Sovereign Military Order of Malta also have a documented presence.
Niger.imp: Nigeriens live under a military government whose security now relies on a foreign force answering to Moscow. A mayor caught with cocaine shows that elected local offices can be used by traffickers. With no recorded outcome, residents cannot tell whether such officials are punished. Families at Gülen schools saw them change hands at Turkey's request.

Nigeria.d: Foreign oil and commodity firms have paid Nigerian officials for oil business. Glencore, a Swiss-based commodity trader, admitted in London that it bribed officials in Nigeria and four other African states. A London judge found that the firm P&ID bribed a petroleum ministry lawyer to win an arbitration award of over $11 billion, and set the award aside. A Milan court acquitted Eni and Shell over the $1.1 billion paid for the OPL 245 oil block. A Shell executive told the US ambassador that Shell had seconded staff to all the relevant ministries. Shell rejected that claim. In Edo State, leaked papers seen by the BBC suggest a confraternity was paid to 'protect votes' and given government posts in return. The BBC linked that group, the Neo Black Movement, to Black Axe, which police in several countries treat as an organised crime group. The movement denies the link. In Abuja, Abba Kyari, a senior police intelligence commander, is on trial for swapping seized cocaine. At Lagos airport, a cargo manager was convicted of trafficking ephedrine. Cambridge Analytica, a British data firm, and Team Jorge, an Israeli group, worked to re-elect President Goodluck Jonathan. Yemi Osinbajo, a senior pastor of the Redeemed Christian Church of God, a Nigerian Pentecostal church, served as vice-president. Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala went from a World Bank managing director post to finance minister. The constitution bars members of secret societies from elected office.
Nigeria.imp: Oil deals won with bribes cost the public money that could pay for schools and clinics. Had the P&ID award stood, the treasury would have owed over $11 billion. In Edo, former members told the BBC that politicians hire confraternity members for election violence, so voters face intimidation at the polls. When a police intelligence commander is charged with swapping seized cocaine, residents cannot rely on drug units to enforce the law.

Rwanda.d: The Tony Blair Institute for Global Change, a London-based non-profit that places advisers inside governments, works in the offices of Rwanda's President and Prime Minister. It has supported two units there, a Strategy and Policy Unit and a Government Action Coordination Unit. It also worked on Imihigo, Rwanda's system of performance contracts. These units plan government priorities and track whether ministries deliver them. The institute reports work with governments in more than 45 countries. Its largest donor is Larry Ellison's foundation, which gave over £52 million in 2023, according to The Guardian. The advisers are employed by the institute, not by the Rwandan state. Three other outside organisations are recorded as present in Rwanda. They are Opus Dei, a Catholic organisation of lay members and priests, NSO Group, an Israeli maker of phone spyware, and British American Tobacco. No case links any of them to a Rwandan office or official. The World Economic Forum, the Davos meeting of political and business leaders, is thought to be active but is not documented. Rwanda is in the Moderate band of the Global Organized Crime Index.
Rwanda.imp: Advisers paid by a foreign-funded institute work on the plans and performance targets of the government Rwandans live under. They answer to their employer in London, not to voters. Residents can read the programme descriptions the institute chooses to publish. They have no public way to see what advice was given or how the donors' money shaped it.

Sao Tome and Principe.d: Nothing is documented yet for São Tomé and Príncipe, so this is a best guess. No case shows an outside government, company, crime group or lodge paying officials or placing people in office here. The only outside organisation recorded as present is the Sovereign Military Order of Malta, a Catholic order that has diplomatic relations with many states and runs medical and aid work. Its presence is lawful and is not evidence of wrongdoing. The Global Organized Crime Index places the country in its Low band. A lack of documented cases means none has come to light, not that none exists.
Sao Tome and Principe.imp: With no documented case, the cost to residents is unknown. The Low band suggests officials here face less outside pressure than in many states. Residents are best protected when they can see who funds officials, who wins public contracts and who owns the companies that do business with the state.

Senegal.d: In Touba, the holy city of the Mouride Brotherhood, a Sufi order with millions of followers, the brotherhood has run its own affairs with wide autonomy since 1928. Senegal's presidents visit its leader, the Khalife général. President Bassirou Diomaye Faye called on Khalife Serigne Mountakha Mbacké two weeks after taking office and again before the Grand Magal pilgrimage. He pledged state help with Touba's water and sanitation. His predecessor Abdoulaye Wade went to Touba the day after his election and appointed Mourides to his government. The government closed more than a dozen schools linked to the Gülen movement, a Turkish religious network that Turkey's government pursues abroad, after requests from Turkey. Turkey's state Maarif Foundation took over the schools and opened its own. While serving as president, Macky Sall accepted the Sunhak Peace Prize, which is funded by the Unification Church, a Korean-founded church, and carries a $1 million award. Jeune Afrique reported that Wade had been initiated into Freemasonry. Wade's camp said Sall was a Freemason too, which Sall denied. Membership of a lodge is lawful. A deputy of the governing coalition was arrested in a cocaine operation. His immunity was lifted, but the case ended without a verdict.
Senegal.imp: Spending on Touba's water and sanitation before the Magal is agreed between the president and a religious leader whom no one elected. About 3,000 children who attended the closed Gülen schools had their schools handed to a foundation run by the Turkish state. The cocaine case against a sitting deputy ended without a verdict. Residents do not know whether drug money paid any member of parliament.

Seychelles.d: Seychelles registers companies that do business in other countries. KuCoin, a cryptocurrency exchange run by PEKEN Global Limited, was registered there while it served customers in countries where it held no licence. The United States imposed a $297 million penalty on it for failing to run effective anti-money-laundering checks. It also failed to report suspicious transactions. US prosecutors separately indicted its executives under the Bank Secrecy Act, a US law that requires firms handling money to report suspicious transfers. They were also charged with moving money without a licence. An exchange that skips these checks lets criminals move money across borders without questions. The case came to light through US enforcement. The Sovereign Military Order of Malta, a Catholic order with diplomatic status that runs medical and aid work, is also recorded as present in Seychelles. Its presence is lawful. No case links any outside group to a Seychelles official or office. Seychelles is in the Low band of the Global Organized Crime Index.
Seychelles.imp: When a company registered in Seychelles is penalised for moving criminal money, foreign banks may treat other Seychelles firms as higher risk. That can raise fees and slow payments for honest local businesses and for families sending or receiving money. The penalty in the KuCoin case went to the United States, so residents gained nothing from it.

Sierra Leone.d: Reuters reported that Jos Leijdekkers, a Dutch cocaine trafficker sentenced in absentia in Rotterdam to 24 years, has 'high-level protection' in Sierra Leone. Facial-recognition matches placed him behind President Julius Maada Bio at a New Year mass in Bio's home town. Sources told Reuters that he is married to the president's daughter, Agnes. The government said the president did not know him and that it was investigating. The head of the immigration service was dismissed after footage showed him with Leijdekkers. Dutch prosecutors said he had lived in the country for months. In 2008 a plane carrying about 700 kilograms of cocaine, painted with Red Cross markings, landed at Lungi airport. Courts convicted airport and security staff along with the foreign crew. The transport and aviation minister was dismissed after the case suggested he had cleared the landing. That allegation was never tried. The Tony Blair Institute, a London non-profit that places advisers inside governments, is recorded as working in Sierra Leone. So is the Sovereign Military Order of Malta, a Catholic order with diplomatic status. The United Grand Lodge of England, Britain's main Masonic body, is thought to have members here, but this is not documented. Sierra Leone is in the High band of the Global Organized Crime Index.
Sierra Leone.imp: If a wanted trafficker is protected through the president's family, as Reuters reported, police and immigration officers have little reason to act against him. A plane carrying cocaine landed at the national airport, and airport staff went to prison. The minister accused of clearing the landing was dismissed but never tried. Residents cannot tell from the courts how high the payments went.

Somalia.d: Turkey's state Maarif Foundation took over the schools in Somalia that were linked to the Gülen movement. The Gülen movement, also called Hizmet, is a Turkish religious network. Turkey's government calls it 'FETÖ' and presses other governments to close its schools. The handover followed talks through Turkey's Foreign Ministry and was complete by June 2017. Families who used those schools now deal with a school operator owned by a foreign state. Several other outside organisations are recorded as present in Somalia. The Muslim Brotherhood is a transnational Islamist movement founded in Egypt. Security companies founded by Erik Prince, the American who started Blackwater, are recorded as working here. The Sovereign Military Order of Malta is a Catholic order with diplomatic status that runs medical and aid work. No documented case shows any of these groups paying Somali officials or placing people in Somali offices. Their presence alone is not evidence of wrongdoing. Somalia is in the Severe band of the Global Organized Crime Index.
Somalia.imp: Teachers and families tied to the Gülen schools saw them handed to a body run by the Turkish state, after a deal between governments. Somalia sits in the Severe band of an organised crime index. That means residents have few working courts, police or watchdogs to check what outside groups or governments do through local officials.

South Africa.d: The Gupta brothers, Indian-born businessmen, built a network that paid and appointed officials during Jacob Zuma's presidency. Deputy finance minister Mcebisi Jonas said they offered him the finance minister's post shortly before Zuma sacked Nhlanhla Nene. The Guptas deny it. The Zondo Commission, a judicial inquiry, found that ministers and heads of the state power and rail companies, Eskom and Transnet, acted corruptly for the family. The United States sanctioned the brothers, who moved to Dubai, and the UAE refused to extradite two of them. The commission found the US consultancy Bain helped take over the tax service, SARS. McKinsey, ABB and SAP admitted in US settlements that they bribed officials at Eskom, Transnet or city councils. Bell Pottinger, a London PR firm, ran fake social-media accounts for a Gupta company and was expelled from its industry body. In KwaZulu-Natal, the provincial police commissioner alleged that the police minister worked with a criminal syndicate. The minister denies it, and an inquiry is under way. In Durban, Gauteng and the Cape, extortion groups calling themselves 'business forums' demand a share of construction contracts and pressure ward councillors. A former national police commissioner, Jackie Selebi, was convicted of taking payments from a drug trafficker. Zuma and the French arms firm Thales face trial over an arms deal; both deny the charges. ANC leaders attend a party school in Tanzania funded by China's Communist Party. Under apartheid, every prime minister and state president belonged to the Afrikaner Broederbond, a secret Afrikaner men's society. Earlier, Alfred Milner's young Oxford staff ran the Transvaal colonial government and argued for the Union of South Africa.
South Africa.imp: Bribes paid to win Eskom and Transnet contracts came out of the companies that supply electricity and run freight rail. McKinsey repaid about R1 billion to Eskom. Builders who refuse the business forums see their sites shut down. One estimate puts the cost of extortion at about 0.7% of GDP a year. With the police minister and national commissioner under investigation, residents have less reason to trust the police.

South Sudan.d: In Juba, Uganda's army sent special forces to protect President Salva Kiir while his government detained ministers allied with First Vice President Riek Machar. Uganda's army chief, Muhoozi Kainerugaba, said the army 'recognises only Salva Kiir'. He said any move against Kiir would be treated as a declaration of war on Uganda. Uganda's parliament later approved the deployment. South Sudan at first denied the troops were there. Benjamin Bol Mel, a businessman close to Kiir, was made a vice-president and deputy secretary-general of the ruling SPLM party. The United States had sanctioned him under its corruption sanctions programme years earlier. A presidential decree removed him from both posts nine months later. Glencore, a Swiss-based commodity trader, admitted paying bribes in South Sudan and four other African states. The Atlas Network, a US-based group of free-market think tanks, is recorded as present. So are influence networks run by several foreign governments, and the Sovereign Military Order of Malta, a Catholic order with diplomatic status. South Sudan is in the Severe band of the Global Organized Crime Index.
South Sudan.imp: Ugandan soldiers now guard South Sudan's president, so South Sudanese voters and institutions have less say over who governs. A businessman under US corruption sanctions served as vice-president until a decree removed him. Bribes paid by commodity traders for oil deals benefit officials, not the public that owns the oil.

Sudan.d: Sudan's army and the Rapid Support Forces, a paramilitary that grew out of Bashir-era militias, have been at war since April 2023. UN experts found 'credible' evidence that the United Arab Emirates flew weapons to the Rapid Support Forces through Amdjarass in Chad. The UAE denies it. The US Treasury says Iran's Revolutionary Guards trained and armed the al-Baraa bin Malik Brigade, an Islamist militia fighting beside the army. Washington sanctioned the brigade and Finance Minister Gebreil Ibrahim, whose movement it tied to Islamist leader Hassan al-Turabi. A sanction is one government's decision, not a court verdict. The United States also sanctioned Meroe Gold, a Sudanese gold miner linked to Yevgeny Prigozhin, founder of Russia's Wagner group. It said the network tried to help suppress the 2018–19 protests for democratic reform. Captagon pill factories have been found in Khartoum, Blue Nile and Jabal Awliya. Turkey's state Maarif Foundation took over the schools linked to the Gülen movement, a Turkish religious network. Omar al-Bashir took power in a coup organised with the National Islamic Front, a Muslim Brotherhood offshoot. After his fall, a committee dismissed judges and prosecutors appointed under him. The High Court overturned those dismissals. Ali Karti, Bashir's foreign minister, now leads the Islamic Movement and is under US, Canadian and EU sanctions.
Sudan.imp: According to UN experts and the US Treasury, foreign states have armed forces on both sides of the war fought in Sudanese towns. The US says a gold firm tied to Russia's Wagner group helped suppress the protests that sought civilian rule. Judges removed for ties to the old regime were ordered back to work. Residents seeking justice may face judges appointed under Bashir.

Tanzania.d: In Kibaha, the Mwalimu Julius Nyerere Leadership School trains party officials from six ruling parties, including Tanzania's CCM. China's Communist Party paid for it with a $40 million grant from its Central Party School, and Chinese party theorists teach there. The school opened in 2022. The other parties are South Africa's ANC, Angola's MPLA, Mozambique's FRELIMO, Namibia's SWAPO and Zimbabwe's ZANU-PF. The Chinese party gains a place where it can teach its methods to the people who run these governments. Tanzania's president read out a public list of alleged drug traffickers and ordered arrests. The list named a regional commissioner and several public figures. Few prosecutions were completed, and most of those detained were released. The list was an accusation by a head of state, not a court finding. Opus Dei, a Catholic organisation, and the Gülen movement, a Turkish religious network, are recorded as present. BAE Systems, a British arms maker, and British American Tobacco are thought to be active but are not documented. Tanzania is in the Moderate band of the Global Organized Crime Index.
Tanzania.imp: Officials of Tanzania's ruling party are taught in a school paid for by a foreign party. Residents do not vote on what is taught there or who teaches it. The public drug list named people who were never tried. Residents learned neither who was guilty nor whether officials protect traffickers. People named on the list carry the accusation without a chance to answer it in court.

Togo.d: Africa Corps, the Russian defence ministry force that replaced the Wagner group in Africa, has soldiers in Togo. President Faure Gnassingbé and Vladimir Putin signed a defence agreement in November 2025. It covers intelligence sharing, arms sales, joint exercises and Russian ships docking at Lomé. The Critical Threats project reports that Africa Corps officers arrived in January 2026. By mid-2026 about 300 to 350 Russian soldiers were in Lomé and at bases in the north. The sanctioned ship Mikhail Britnev unloaded vehicles at Lomé for Africa Corps units in Mali. Russia gains docking rights at Lomé and a supply point for its forces in Mali. Three opposition parties asked for a public debate on foreign troops. NSO Group, an Israeli maker of phone spyware, is recorded as active in Togo. So is Archimedes Group, an Israeli political consulting firm that Facebook banned for fake election campaigns in Africa. The Grand Orient de France and the Grande Loge Nationale Française, two French Masonic bodies, are thought to have members here. That is not documented, and lodge membership is lawful. Togo is in the High band of the Global Organized Crime Index.
Togo.imp: Russian soldiers now work alongside Togo's army under an agreement signed by the president. Opposition parties asked for a public debate on it. Lomé's port also serves as a supply point for Russian forces in Mali, so a port that handles the country's trade is tied to a foreign military operation.

Tunisia.d: Ennahda, a party that grew out of the Muslim Brotherhood tradition, led Tunisia's government after winning the 2011 Constituent Assembly election. It says it has no organisational link to the Egyptian Brotherhood. Its members Hamadi Jebali and Ali Laarayedh served as prime ministers. Rafik Abdessalem, son-in-law of party leader Rached Ghannouchi, was foreign minister. Ghannouchi later became speaker of parliament. He has been in prison since 2023. A court gave him 22 more years for 'plotting against state security' in the Instalingo case. The same court sentenced Abdessalem and former prime minister Hichem Mechichi, who was tried in absentia, to over 30 years each. Ennahda calls the case political. Ghannouchi later received a further 14-year sentence. Several other outside organisations are recorded as present in Tunisia. Hizb ut-Tahrir is a transnational movement that seeks an Islamic caliphate. The Trilateral Commission is a private forum of political and business leaders from North America, Europe and Asia. Archimedes Group is an Israeli political consulting firm that Facebook banned for fake election campaigns. No case links these three to a Tunisian office. Tunisia is in the High band of the Global Organized Crime Index.
Tunisia.imp: Tunisians who voted for Ennahda saw its leaders govern and then receive long prison terms. Whether the convictions punish real plotting or political opposition is disputed, and Ennahda calls the case political. Either way, voters now choose among parties whose former leaders are in prison or abroad. Supporters of Ennahda have lost the people they elected to lead them.

Uganda.d: Huawei technicians working at police headquarters in Kampala helped the police cyber unit get into the encrypted messages of opposition MP Bobi Wine, the Wall Street Journal reported. Huawei, China's largest telecoms equipment maker, denied it. The Journal found no evidence that Huawei's managers in China or the Chinese state directed this. US Christian groups have worked with Ugandan lawmakers. David Bahati chairs Uganda's National Prayer Breakfast Fellowship, linked to The Fellowship, a US Christian network that runs prayer breakfasts for politicians. Journalist Jeff Sharlet reported that Bahati first floated his anti-homosexuality bill, which proposed the death penalty, at a Uganda prayer breakfast. Bahati has been a state minister since 2021. Uganda passed the Anti-Homosexuality Act in 2023, with life imprisonment and in some cases death. A Ugandan activist named Sharon Slater, president of the Arizona-based Family Watch International, as having lobbied for it. The World Bank halted new lending to Uganda over the law. NSO Group, an Israeli maker of phone spyware, is also recorded as present. So are Opus Dei, a Catholic organisation, and the Gülen movement, a Turkish religious network. Uganda is in the High band of the Global Organized Crime Index.
Uganda.imp: Opposition politicians cannot assume their encrypted messages are private if police have foreign technical help. Gay Ugandans face life imprisonment under a law that a foreign lobby group is reported to have promoted. The World Bank's halt on new lending cut funds for public projects that all residents use, including those who had no part in passing the law.

Zambia.d: Zambia's constitution declares it a Christian nation. President Edgar Lungu turned a religious-affairs desk into a full Ministry of National Guidance and Religious Affairs. He appointed Rev. Godfridah Sumaili, a cleric, as a nominated member of parliament and made her the minister. She held the post for five years. After the 2021 election, President Hichilema folded the ministry into a department of the Vice-President's office. Pentecostal and evangelical church networks are recorded as active in Zambia. So is the Universal Church of the Kingdom of God, a Brazilian-founded church. Huawei, China's largest telecoms equipment maker, is recorded as present. The Wall Street Journal reported that Huawei staff helped Zambia's government spy on people inside the country; Huawei denied it. SCL Group, the parent of the British data firm Cambridge Analytica, is also recorded as present. The United Grand Lodge of England, Britain's main Masonic body, and the defunct bank BCCI are thought to have been active, but this is not documented. Zambia is in the Moderate band of the Global Organized Crime Index.
Zambia.imp: For five years one faith had its own ministry and a cleric in the cabinet. Zambians of other faiths, or none, had no equal place in government. If Huawei staff helped the government monitor residents, as reported, Zambians cannot be sure their phone calls and messages are private. Opposition figures and journalists have the most to lose.

Zimbabwe.d: Kudakwashe Tagwirei, founder of Sakunda Holdings, became a cabinet minister in October 2026. President Mnangagwa appointed him Minister of Economic Development and Investment Promotion. Sakunda grew through fuel trading with the commodity trader Trafigura and a state agriculture contract called Command Agriculture. The government paid Sakunda in Treasury bills. The United States sanctioned Tagwirei, accusing him of misappropriating public funds and supporting senior officials. Britain later sanctioned him too. He denies the allegations. The ruling party, ZANU-PF, had already co-opted him onto its Central Committee.
